display: The Light of Asia, Book the Second
text:
Lo! as hid seed shoots after rainless years,
So good and evil, pains and pleasures, hates
And loves, and all dead deeds, come forth again
Bearing bright leaves or dark, sweet fruit or sour.
note: Past actions bear fruit later; consequences of deeds

tags.when_helps: Someone reflecting on how past deeds, good or bad, come back to bear fruit.

display_text:
Lo! as hid seed shoots after rainless years,
So good and evil, pains and pleasures, hates
And loves, and all dead deeds, come forth again
Bearing bright leaves or dark, sweet fruit or sour.
plain: Just as hidden seed sprouts after years without rain, so good and evil, pains and pleasures, hates and loves, and all past deeds return, bearing bright or dark leaves, sweet or sour fruit.
core_idea: Past deeds return like seeds that sprout

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Third
text:
We are the voices of the wandering wind,
Which moan for rest and rest can never find;
Lo! as the wind is so is mortal life,
A moan, a sigh, a sob, a storm, a strife.
Wherefore and whence we are ye cannot know,
Nor where life springs nor whither life doth go;
We are as ye are, ghosts from the inane,
What pleasure have we of our changeful pain?
note: Restlessness and impermanence of life

tags.when_helps: Someone feeling life is restless and unanswerable, wanting company in that uncertainty.

display_text:

plain: We are voices of the wandering wind, longing for rest and never finding it. Mortal life is like that wind: a moan, a sob, a storm. No one knows where life comes from or goes.
core_idea: Life is restless and changing like the wind

plain_judge.issue: Drops "we are as ye are, ghosts from the inane" and changeful pain lines.

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Third
text:
Nay, though we locked up love and life with lips
So close that night and day our breaths grew one
Time would thrust in between to filch away
My passion and thy grace, as black Night steals
The rose-gleams from you peak, which fade to grey
And are not seen to fade.
note: Ageing and time wearing away love

tags.when_helps: Someone deeply in love who feels the ache that time will change even the closest bond.

display_text:

plain: Even if we held love and life so close that our breaths became one, time would still come between us and steal away my passion and your beauty, just as night quietly takes the rosy light from a mountain peak.
core_idea: Time steals even the closest love

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Third
text:
The high and low, the good and bad, must die,
And then, 't is taught, begin anew and live
Somewhere, somehow,--who knows?--and so again
The pangs, the parting, and the lighted pile--
Such is man's round.
note: Mortality comes to everyone; the cycle of loss

tags.when_helps: Someone confronting that everyone must die and wondering what comes after.

display_text:

plain: High and low, good and bad, all must die, and then, it is taught, begin again somewhere, somehow, who knows; and so again come the pain, the parting, and the funeral fire. Such is the human cycle.
core_idea: All die and the cycle of rebirth repeats

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Third
text:
Oh! suffering world,
Oh! known and unknown of my common flesh,
Caught in this common net of death and woe,
And life which binds to both! I see, I feel
The vastness of the agony of earth,
The vainness of its joys, the mockery
Of all its best, the anguish of its worst;
Since pleasures end in pain, and youth in age,
And love in loss, and life in hateful death,
And death in unknown lives, which will but yoke
Men to their wheel again to whirl the round
Of false delights and woes that are not false.
note: Awakening to the shared suffering and impermanence of life

tags.when_helps: Someone overwhelmed by the scale of the world's suffering who wants it named with compassion.

core_idea: The world is caught in a wheel of suffering

plain_judge.issue: Drops mockery of earth's best and "woes that are not false".

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Fourth
text:
Men
Perished in winter-winds till one smote fire
From flint-stones coldly hiding what they held,
The red spark treasured from the kindling sun.
They gorged on flesh like wolves, till one sowed corn,
Which grew a weed, yet makes the life of man;
They mowed and babbled till some tongue struck speech,
And patient fingers framed the lettered sound.
What good gift have my brothers but it came
From search and strife and loving sacrifice?
note: Every good gift comes from effort and sacrifice

tags.when_helps: Someone wondering if effort and sacrifice are worth it, reminded that every human gift came from them.

core_idea: Every human gift came from struggle and sacrifice

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Fourth
text:
Friend, that love is false
Which clings to love for selfish sweets of love;
But I, who love these more than joys of mine--
Yea, more than joy of theirs--depart to save
Them and all flesh, if utmost love avail.
note: True love versus clinging, selfish love; painful leaving

tags.when_helps: Someone questioning whether their love is selfish, drawn to a love that serves others first.

display_text:

plain: Friend, love that clings to love for its own pleasures is false. I love these people more than my joy, even more than theirs, so I leave to save them and all beings, if utmost love can.
core_idea: True love is selfless, not clinging

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Fifth
text:
Will ye, for love of soul, so loathe your flesh,
So scourge and maim it, that it shall not serve
To bear the spirit on, searching for home,
But founder on the track before nightfall,
Like willing steed o'er-spurred? Will ye, sad sirs,
Dismantle and dismember this fair house,
Where we have come to dwell by painful pasts;
Whose windows give us light--the little light
Whereby we gaze abroad to know if dawn
Will break, and whither winds the better road?
note: Harsh self-punishment; caring for the body on the path

tags.when_helps: Someone pushing themselves too hard in the name of discipline who needs to treat the body kindly.

display_text:

core_idea: Don't destroy the body the spirit needs

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Fifth
text:
O, ye palms, which rise
Eager to pierce the sky and drink the wind
Blown from Malaya and the cool blue seas,
What secret know ye that ye grow content,
From time of tender shoot to time of fruit,
Murmuring such sun-songs from your feathered crowns?
Ye, too, who dwell so merry in the trees--
Quick-darting parrots, bee-birds, bulbuls, doves--
None of ye hate your life, none of ye deem
To strain to better by foregoing needs!
note: Contentment; not hating one's own life

tags.when_helps: Someone straining to improve themselves who might learn contentment from trees and birds.

core_idea: Nature lives content without self-denial

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Fifth
text:
He thou lovest slept
Dead on thy bosom yesterday: today
Thou know'st the whole wide world weeps with thy woe
The grief which all hearts share grows less for one.
note: Grief after a death; sorrow shared by all

tags.when_helps: Someone freshly bereaved who needs to know the whole world shares this grief.

display_text:

The grief which all hearts share grows less for one.
plain: Yesterday the one you love died in your arms; today you know the whole world weeps with you. A grief that all hearts share grows lighter for each one.
core_idea: Shared grief grows lighter

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Sixth
text:
Pity and need
Make all flesh kin. There is no caste in blood,
Which runneth of one hue, nor caste in tears,
Which trickle salt with all; neither comes man
To birth with tilka-mark stamped on the brow,
Nor sacred thread on neck. Who doth right deeds
Is twice-born, and who doeth ill deeds vile.
note: Feeling lesser or excluded; shared humanity, worth by deeds

tags.when_helps: Someone judged by birth or status who needs to hear worth comes from deeds, not caste.

display_text:

core_idea: Deeds, not birth, make a person noble

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Sixth
note: Balance; overstraining versus slackness, burnout

tags.when_helps: Someone pushing too hard or slacking too much who needs a reminder of balance.

plain: A string pulled too tight snaps and the music is gone; a string too loose makes no sound. Tune us like a sitar, neither too low nor too high.
core_idea: Balance, not extremes, makes life work

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Sixth
text:
Also I think that good must come of good
And ill of evil--surely--unto all--
In every place and time--seeing sweet fruit
Groweth from wholesome roots, and bitter things
From poison-stocks; yea, seeing, too, how spite
Breeds hate, and kindness friends, and patience peace
Even while we live; and when 't is willed we die
Shall there not be as good a `Then' as `Now'?
note: Kindness and patience bear fruit; trust about death

tags.when_helps: Someone uneasy about death who finds comfort that kindness bears fruit now and after.

display_text:

Shall there not be as good a `Then' as `Now'?
plain: I believe good comes from good and evil from evil, everywhere: sweet fruit from healthy roots, hate from spite, friends from kindness, peace from patience. So after death, will the future not be as good as now?
core_idea: Good brings good, now and after death

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Sixth
text:
Even as one,
At rest upon a mountain-summit, marks
His path wind up by precipice and crag
Past thick-set woods shrunk to a patch; through bogs
Glittering false-green; down hollows where he toiled
Breathless; on dizzy ridges where his feet
Had well-nigh slipped; beyond the sunny lawns,
The cataract and the cavern and the pool,
Backward to those dim flats wherefrom he sprang
To reach the blue--thus Buddha did behold
Life's upward steps long-linked, from levels low
Where breath is base, to higher slopes and higher
Whereon the ten great Virtues wait to lead
The climber skyward.
note: Looking back on a hard road; growth through struggle

tags.when_helps: Someone tired from a long climb who could look back and see how far they have come.

core_idea: Life is a long upward climb toward virtue

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Sixth
text:
Many a House of Life
Held me--Seeking Ever Him Wrought
These Prisons of the Senses, Sorrow-Fraught;
Sore was My Ceaseless Strife! But Now,
Thou Builder of this Tabernacle--Thou!
I Know Thee! Never Shalt Thou Build Again
These Walls of Pain, Nor Raise the Roof-Tree of Deceits, Nor Lay
Fresh Rafters on the Clay:
Broken Thy House is, and the Ridge-Pole Split!
Delusion Fashioned it!
Safe Pass I Thence--Deliverance to Obtain.
note: Breaking free from craving and self-made suffering

tags.when_helps: Someone who has finally seen through a craving or delusion and feels freed.

display_text:
Many a House of Life

I Know Thee! Never Shalt Thou Build Again

plain: Through many lives I sought the builder of these sorrowful prisons of the senses. Now, builder, I know you; you will never build these walls of pain again. Delusion made your house, and it is broken. I go free.
core_idea: Seeing through delusion ends the cycle of suffering

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Seventh
text:
Evil swells the debts to pay,
Good delivers and acquits;
Shun evil, follow good; hold sway
Over thyself. This is the Way.
note: Choosing good, self-mastery; a simple way to live

tags.when_helps: Someone unsure how to live who wants the simplest possible rule: shun evil, do good, govern yourself.

display_text:
Evil swells the debts to pay,
Good delivers and acquits;
Shun evil, follow good; hold sway
Over thyself. This is the Way.
plain: Evil adds to the debts you must pay; good frees and clears you. Avoid evil, do good, and rule over yourself. This is the Way.
core_idea: Shun evil, do good, master yourself

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Seventh
text:
The greater beareth with the lesser love
So it may raise it unto easier heights.
Take heed that no man, being 'soaped from bonds,
Vexeth bound souls with boasts of liberty.
Free are ye rather that your freedom spread
By patient winning and sweet wisdom's skill.
note: Patience and humility toward those still struggling

tags.when_helps: Someone who has grown and is tempted to look down on those still struggling.

display_text:
The greater beareth with the lesser love
So it may raise it unto easier heights.
Take heed that no man, being 'scaped from bonds,
Vexeth bound souls with boasts of liberty.

By patient winning and sweet wisdom's skill.
plain: A greater love bears patiently with a lesser one to lift it higher. Whoever has escaped bondage should not taunt those still bound. Be free so that you spread freedom through patience and gentle wisdom.
core_idea: Use your freedom to free others patiently

plain_judge.issue: "Free are ye rather that your freedom spread" recast as a command to be free.

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Pray not! the Darkness will not brighten!
Ask Nought from the Silence, for it cannot speak!
Vex not your mournful minds with pious pains!
Ah! Brothers, Sisters! seek Nought from the helpless gods by gift and hymn,
Nor bribe with blood, nor feed with fruit and cakes;
Within yourselves deliverance must be sought;
Each man his prison makes.
note: Freedom must be sought within oneself

tags.when_helps: Someone whose prayers seem unanswered, open to seeking freedom within themselves.

display_text:

plain: Do not pray; the darkness will not lighten and the silence cannot answer. Do not try to buy help from powerless gods with offerings. Freedom must be sought within; each person makes their own prison.
core_idea: Liberation is found within, not from gods

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Nothing endures: fair virtues waste with time,
Foul sins grow purged thereby.
note: Guilt fades with time; nothing is permanent

tags.when_helps: Someone haunted by a past wrong who needs to hear that time changes all things.

display_text:
Nothing endures: fair virtues waste with time,

plain: Nothing lasts: good virtues wear away with time, and bad sins are cleansed by it.
core_idea: Time wears away both virtue and sin

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Ye are not bound! the Soul of Things is sweet,
The Heart of Being is celestial rest;
Stronger than woe is will: that which was Good
Doth pass to Better--Best. I, Buddh, who wept with all my brothers' tears,
Whose heart was broken by a whole world's woe,
Laugh and am glad, for there is Liberty
Ho! ye who suffer! know Ye suffer from yourselves. None else compels
None other holds you that ye live and die,
And whirl upon the wheel, and hug and kiss
Its spokes of agony, Its tire of tears, its nave of nothingness.
note: Hope amid suffering; we are not trapped

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels trapped by suffering and needs to hear that liberation is possible.

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
That which ye sow ye reap. See yonder fields
The sesamum was sesamum, the corn
Was corn. The Silence and the Darkness knew!
So is a man's fate born. He cometh, reaper of the things he sowed,
Sesamum, corn, so much cast in past birth;
And so much weed and poison-stuff, which mar
Him and the aching earth. If he shall labour rightly, rooting these,
And planting wholesome seedlings where they grew,
Fruitful and fair and clean the ground shall be,
And rich the harvest due.
note: Reaping what we sow; changing habits for a better life

tags.when_helps: Someone reckoning with consequences of past choices who wants to plant better ones now.

Purer, with broader gleam.

text:

Dumb to the summons of the true life kept
For him who false puts by.

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
This is peace--
To conquer love of self and lust of life,
To tear deep-rooted passion from the breast,
To still the inward strife; For love, to clasp Eternal Beauty close;
For glory, to be lord of self; for pleasure,
To live beyond the gods; for countless wealth,
To lay up lasting treasure Of perfect service rendered, duties done
In charity, soft speech, and stainless days
These riches shall not fade away in life,
Nor any death dispraise.
note: What true peace and lasting wealth are

tags.when_helps: Someone torn by inner strife and wanting a picture of what real peace and wealth are.

display_text:

core_idea: Peace is mastering self and craving

plain_judge.issue: Drops "for pleasure, to live beyond the gods"; descriptive definition of peace partly turned into commands.

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Manifold tracks lead to yon sister-peaks
Around whose snows the gilded clouds are curled
By steep or gentle slopes the climber comes
Where breaks that other world. Strong limbs may dare the rugged road which storms,
Soaring and perilous, the mountain's breast;
The weak must wind from slower ledge to ledge
With many a place of rest. So is the Eightfold Path which brings to peace;
By lower or by upper heights it goes.
The firm soul hastes, the feeble tarries. All
Will reach the sunlit snows.
note: Slow progress is still progress; everyone arrives

tags.when_helps: Someone who feels slow or weak on their path and needs to hear all will arrive.

text:
Have good-will
To all that lives, letting unkindness die
And greed and wrath; so that your lives be made
Like soft airs passing by.
note: Letting go of anger and unkindness

tags.when_helps: Someone holding unkindness or anger who wants to let it go and live gently.

display_text:
Have good-will
To all that lives, letting unkindness die
And greed and wrath; so that your lives be made
Like soft airs passing by.
plain: Wish well to every living thing, letting unkindness, greed and anger die, so that your lives become like gentle breezes passing by.
core_idea: Goodwill to all; let anger and greed die

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Govern the lips
As they were palace-doors, the King within;
Tranquil and fair and courteous be all words
Which from that presence win.
note: Guarding one's speech; words spoken in anger

situations: conflict with a friend or colleague
tags.when_helps: Someone about to say something harsh who needs a reminder to keep speech courteous.

display_text:
Govern the lips
As they were palace-doors, the King within;
Tranquil and fair and courteous be all words
Which from that presence win.
plain: Guard your lips as if they were palace doors with a king inside; let every word that comes out be calm, kind and courteous.
core_idea: Guard your speech; keep it calm and kind

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Let each act
Assoil a fault or help a merit grow;
Like threads of silver seen through crystal beads
Let love through good deeds show.
note: Making amends; showing love through actions

tags.when_helps: Someone wanting to make amends or grow, through small good deeds done with love.

display_text:
Let each act
Assoil a fault or help a merit grow;
Like threads of silver seen through crystal beads
Let love through good deeds show.
plain: Let each act undo a fault or help some good grow; let love show through good deeds like silver thread through crystal beads.
core_idea: Let every act show love

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
note: Ordinary family life as a path; growing through weakness

tags.when_helps: A person living an ordinary family life who wonders if it can still be a spiritual path.

plain: I know love of spouse and child is dear, friends and pleasures sweet, and life's fears false though strong. Those who must, live such lives, but make your weakness a golden stair, rising through them to lovelier truths.
core_idea: Ordinary life can be a stair to truth

plain_judge.issue: Drops "fruitful of good life's gentle charities".

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Enter the Path! There is no grief like Hate!
No pains like passions, no deceit like sense!
Enter the Path! far hath he gone whose foot
Treads down one fond offence.
note: Hatred as suffering; small steps of change count

tags.when_helps: Someone gripped by hate or passion who needs a push to take one step away from it.

display_text:
Enter the Path! There is no grief like Hate!
No pains like passions, no deceit like sense!
Enter the Path! far hath he gone whose foot
Treads down one fond offence.
plain: Enter the Path! No sorrow is like hatred, no pain like passion, no deceit like the senses. Whoever overcomes even one cherished fault has come far.
core_idea: Overcoming one fault is real progress

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Bear not false witness, slander not, nor lie;
Truth is the speech of inward purity.
note: Honesty; temptation to lie or gossip

tags.when_helps: Someone tempted to lie or gossip who wants a short reminder of honesty.

display_text:
Bear not false witness, slander not, nor lie;
Truth is the speech of inward purity.
plain: Do not bear false witness, slander, or lie; truthful speech comes from a pure heart.
core_idea: Truthful speech reflects inner purity

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
text:
Shun drugs and drinks which work the wit abuse;
Clear minds, clean bodies, need no soma juice.
note: Drinking or drug use; keeping a clear mind

situations: a habit or addiction I can't break
tags.when_helps: Someone struggling with drink or drugs who wants a plain reason to keep a clear mind.

display_text:
Shun drugs and drinks which work the wit abuse;
Clear minds, clean bodies, need no soma juice.
plain: Avoid drugs and drinks that cloud your mind; a clear mind and clean body need no intoxicant.
core_idea: A clear mind needs no intoxicants

display: The Light of Asia, Book the Eighth
note: Love over ritual; caring for family, teachers, friends

tags.when_helps: Someone wanting to honour parents, teachers, family and friends in daily life.

plain: Don't scatter rice as offerings; instead offer loving thoughts and acts to everyone: parents, teachers, spouse and children, friends and all people, the smallest creatures, and the saints and dead above. That shuts out evil and keeps every direction safe.
core_idea: Offer love to all, not ritual offerings

plain_judge.issue: Drops the mapping of each relation to a compass quarter.
